_comment: Engine conventions that asset.check verifies (structure and semantics). Every rule names what it checks,
why (the engine behaviour) and the fix. Numbers are vanilla facts; 'vanilla' says how vanilla models do it.
sev: error = the game shows it wrong or crashes; warn = it looks wrong next to vanilla; info = worth a look.

veh.paint_dirt.what: Paint (key colours paint1/paint2) sits on the dirt texture vehiclegrunge256 (so the car gets dirty and the key colour picks up the grain) or on the model's own body texture (paint jobs, liveries); never on the other shared vehicle.txd textures.
veh.paint_dirt.hint: map the painted faces onto vehiclegrunge256 (vehicle.txd) and keep the key colour as the material colour

veh.lamp_tex.what: Lamp key colours only work on vehiclelights128 (the engine swaps it for vehiclelightson128 when a lamp is on).
veh.lamp_tex.hint: give the lamp materials the texture vehiclelights128 and keep the lamp key colour

veh.env_uv2.what: The body sheen (MatFX env map xvehicleenv128 on the paint) reads UV set 2; a painted geometry with one UV set gets a flat sheen. Vanilla wheels and exhausts carry env with one UV set; only painted geometries are checked.
veh.env_uv2.hint: export the body with two UV sets (DragonFF: UV2 on) or drop the env effect

veh.sheen_missing.what: Paint without the env sheen (MatFX env + reflection material) looks matt next to vanilla cars.
veh.sheen_missing.hint: use the paint material preset (env xvehicleenv128, coefficient and reflection intensity like vanilla)

veh.wheel_scale.what: The game scales the wheel mesh to wheel_scale of the IDE line; the mesh diameter should equal it (vanilla cars 0.99-1.03).
veh.wheel_scale.hint: model the wheel at the IDE wheel_scale diameter (or change wheel_scale)

veh.dummy_side.what: Frames named *_l*/*_r* (wheel_lf_dummy, door_rr_dummy, ...) sit on their side (left x < 0, right x > 0) and ped_arm is on the driver side (x < 0, every vanilla car).
veh.dummy_side.hint: mirror the frame to its side or rename it

veh.bumper_corner.what: bump_front_dummy and bump_rear_dummy sit at a front/rear corner (|x| > 15 % of the width), where the bumper hinges when damaged (125 of 132 vanilla cars).
veh.bumper_corner.hint: put the bumper dummy at the corner where the bumper hangs from

veh.frames.what: Frames every vanilla model of the type has; the engine looks them up by name (critical ones are errors, the others warnings).
veh.frames.hint: add the frame (satk kit template --like <vanilla model> builds the full tree)

veh.frame_parent.what: Parts hang from the same parent frame as in vanilla (<root> = the clump root frame).
veh.frame_parent.hint: reparent the frame like the vanilla model

geom.normals.what: Vehicles, peds and weapons need vertex normals (the game lights them per vertex).

geom.prelit.what: Map models carry prelight (vertex colours); without it they render too bright or black.
geom.prelit.hint: bake prelight (satk blender game-ready) and export vertex colours

ide.draw_hd_col.what: An HD map model with collision has draw distance <= 300; above 300 the engine treats it as a big building (no collision streaming).
ide.draw_hd_col.hint: set draw distance <= 300 and give the model a LOD for the distance

col.face_light.what: Collision face light 0 makes peds and cars on it about 3x darker by day (ambient only).
col.face_light.hint: take face light from the prelight (satk col gen derives it)

col.missing.what: Vehicles carry an embedded COL3 (spheres + mesh + shadow mesh).

txd.vehicle_format.what: Vehicle, ped and weapon textures are DXT1/DXT3 (or 32-bit) with one mip level; vanilla never uses DXT5 there.
